id: title:andrewm4894:keep malformed links from crashing markdown stripping

review.posthog_relevance: Resilience of markdown rendering in the frontend, allowing malformed URLs to display safely without crashing the browser.
review.reason: The implementation P1.F2.H1 adds a try-catch around URL resolution. This demonstrates a bounded, localized improvement: it prevents browser crashes or broken link rendering when a URL constructor throws an exception, while retaining existing stripping of dangerous protocols. This is a substantive, bounded reliability improvement.
review.uncertainty: The score is 1 because the change is a localized maintenance and behavior correction rather than a broader systemic capability or a critical path dependency. No adoption or incident avoidance is demonstrated.

observations.limitations: This chunk contains two hunks. P1.F1.H1 is a test file; P1.F2.H1 is the implementation. The implementation change is complete and demonstrates the behavior. P1.F1.H1 is not a production change and should not be scored. P1.F2.H1 is scored. No other hunks exist in this chunk.

observations.behavior: Adds a try-catch around URL resolution; if URL constructor throws, returns the raw href instead of crashing.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows markdown links with malformed URLs (e.g., missing host, invalid port) to render as plain text rather than crashing the browser or displaying a broken link, while still stripping dangerous protocols. This preserves user experience for edge cases without changing the stripping of bold/italic/code.
